# render


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

One runtime draws a spec everywhere. A host element carries the spec as
inert JSON, and the runtime mounts it:

``` html
<div data-rupaka><script type="application/json">{...spec...}</script></div>
```

The runtime boots on load and after each htmx swap. Nothing is templated
into the script.

## The bundle

[`bundle`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/board.html#bundle) joins
the core, the fns, the blocks and the boot script in a fixed order. The
style sheet starts with `paper.css`, the tokens of the paper theme,
which the side panel of the board (`rupaka.board`) uses too. There is no
bundler and no build step.

### assets

``` python
def assets()->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The files of the runtime, in bundle order.*

The script starts with the core and ends with the boot. Each block is in
it.

``` python
js = bundle()
assert js.startswith('/* static/rupaka.js */') and js.rstrip().endswith('})();')
for n in manifests(): assert f"Rupaka.block('{n}'" in js, n
assert 'eval(' not in js and 'new Function' not in js and 'fetch(' not in js
assert f"version: '{__version__}'" in js and '{{version}}' not in js
```

Each block style uses only the `--rk-*` vars for colour, so a demo takes
the look of the page that holds it.

``` python
import re
```

``` python
for p in assets().css[2:]:   # the blocks: paper.css and rupaka.css hold the colours
    cols = re.findall(r'(?:#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}\b|rgba?\(|hsl\()', p.read_text())
    test_eq((p.name, cols), (p.name, []))
```

## three.js for scenes

A [`scene`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#scene) block
draws in 3D with three.js. rupaka keeps a copy of three.js in
`rupaka/static/vendor/three/`, so a scene works offline and loads
nothing from a CDN.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>item</th>
<th>value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>version</td>
<td>three 0.185.0, from npm (<code>three-0.185.0.tgz</code>, integrity
<code>sha512-+yRrcRO2iZa8uzvNNl0d7cL4huhgKgBvVJ0njcTe8xFqZ6DMAFZdCKDP91SEAuj25bNAj7k1QQdf+srZywVK6w==</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>files</td>
<td><code>three.core.min.js</code> and <code>three.module.min.js</code>,
as npm gives them, with no change</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>licence</td>
<td>MIT, in <code>vendor/three/LICENSE</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>size</td>
<td>about 750 KB</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

0.185.0 is the last release that has the minified files. The tests check
the hash of each file, so a changed file fails at once.

The hashes of the two files, as `sha256`:

``` python
for f, h in THREE.files.items(): test_eq(hashlib.sha256((VENDOR/'three'/f).read_bytes()).hexdigest(), h)
assert 'MIT License' in (VENDOR/'three'/'LICENSE').read_text()
```

The two files are ES modules: the second one imports the first. A module
cannot load from `file://` or from a sandboxed `srcdoc` frame, and those
are places where rupaka draws. So
[`three_js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#three_js)
joins the two files into one classic script. It changes only the
`import` and `export` statements: an import becomes a read from the
first file’s names, and an export becomes a `return`. The script puts
the names on `window.RupakaTHREE`, and it does nothing when it runs a
second time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### three_js

``` python
def three_js()->str:
```

*three.js as one classic script that sets `window.RupakaTHREE`, made
from the two vendored module files.*

The script has no module statement left, and it exports the names that a
scene uses.

``` python
t = three_js()
assert not re.search(r'(^|[;}])\s*(import|export)\s*[{*]', t) and 'from"./three' not in t
for k in ('WebGLRenderer', 'MeshToonMaterial', 'ExtrudeGeometry', 'DepthTexture', 'REVISION'): assert f'{k}:' in t, k
test_eq(bundle('three'), t)
```

## The host element

[`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#host) writes
the element that carries a spec. JSON in a `<script>` must not hold
`</script>`, so every `<` becomes `\u003c`. `JSON.parse` reads it back
as `<`.

## A static page

[`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page) writes
one self-contained HTML file: the runtime, the style, the specs, and
abhyasa’s palette. The `fonts` argument picks how the page gets its
fonts:

### page

``` python
def page(
    specs, title:str=None, fonts:str='link', lead:str='', theme:str=None, askable:bool=None
)->str:
```

*One self-contained HTML document that draws `specs`, with no network.*

A page loads nothing from the network: no `src`, `href` or `url()`
points at `http`. (The SVG namespace string is not a request.) With
`fonts='none'` it has no `@font-face` rule.

``` python
spec = dict(rupaka=1, id='t', title='T', state=dict(a=1), blocks=[dict(type='readout', text='{a}')])
p = page(spec)
assert not re.search(r'''(src|href)=["']?https?:|url\(\s*["']?https?:''', p)
assert '@font-face' in p and '@font-face' not in page(spec, fonts='none')
assert 'data:font/woff2;base64,' in page(spec, fonts='embed')
assert 'window.RupakaTHREE=' not in p
s3 = page(dict(rupaka=1, id='s', state={}, blocks=[dict(type='scene', blocks=[])]), fonts='none')
assert 'window.RupakaTHREE=' in s3 and not re.search(r'''(src|href)=["']?https?:|url\(\s*["']?https?:''', s3)
```

### The paper theme

The paper theme gives a demo a warm paper ground, light boxes, sketch
lines and a hand font, as on a teacher’s board. It is always light. A
host puts `data-rk-theme="paper"` on the demo element or on a parent.
[`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#host),
[`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page) and
[`Demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#demo) take
`theme='paper'`. The hand font is Patrick Hand, under the SIL Open Font
License, in `static/fonts` with its licence. A host that serves the
fonts loads it with
[`font_css`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#font_css).

``` python
pp = page(spec, fonts='none', theme='paper')
assert '<div data-rupaka data-rk-theme="paper">' in pp and '<div data-rupaka>' in page(spec, fonts='none')
assert "font-family: 'Patrick Hand'" in font_css() and all((STATIC/'fonts'/f).exists() for *_, f, _ in FONTS)
assert 'Patrick Hand' in (STATIC/'fonts'/'LICENSES.txt').read_text()
```

### Ask about this: the rk-ask event

Each demo shows a small “Ask about this” control at its end. The learner
clicks it, can type a question, and clicks Ask (or pushes Enter). The
demo then sends the `rk-ask` event, as a gate sends `rk-predict`. The
event bubbles, crosses a shadow root and is cancelable. Its `detail` is
plain JSON:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>key</th>
<th>what it is</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#demo"><code>demo</code></a></td>
<td>the <code>id</code> of the spec</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>text</code></td>
<td>the words of the learner, at most 500 characters; it can be
empty</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>state</code></td>
<td>the input keys (the keys of <code>spec.state</code>) and their
values now, as <code>Rupaka.state</code> gives them. A string has at
most 200 characters, and a list or an object at most 50 items, 3 levels
deep.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>step</code></td>
<td>the state key <code>step</code> of an explainer, else the id of the
first open gate, else <code>null</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The event never holds derived values, gate answers, DOM or HTML. A host
that takes the ask calls `preventDefault`. Then the demo says “Sent to
the tutor.”, else “No tutor is on this page.” A host can send the same
event with `Rupaka.ask(el, text)`, for example from a voice command. It
gives false when a listener called `preventDefault`.

The control is on by default. A spec turns it off with
`"askable": false`. The host page can turn it on or off for one render,
and the host switch comes first. For example, a talk shows the control
in the editor but not in the window that the room sees.
[`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#host),
[`page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page) and
[`Demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#demo) take
`askable=True` or `askable=False`, which writes `data-rk-askable` on the
element. `Rupaka.mount(el, spec, {askable})` does the same. With
`askable` not set, the spec decides. In every case the event is the
same.

``` python
assert '<div data-rupaka>' in page(spec, fonts='none')
assert '<div data-rupaka data-rk-askable="false">' in page(spec, fonts='none', askable=False)
assert '<div data-rupaka data-rk-theme="paper" data-rk-askable="true">' in host(spec, 'paper', askable=1)
```

## Notebooks: show

`show(spec)` returns an object that a notebook draws. It gives two mime
types:

- `application/vnd.rupaka+json`: the spec, for a frontend that knows
  rupaka (a later leela change).
- `text/html`: the whole page with `fonts='none'`. leela, Jupyter and VS
  Code draw it in a sandboxed frame. This works in leela today.

## Markdown: md

`md(spec)` writes a ```` ```rupaka ```` fence with readable JSON. A
renderer that knows rupaka mounts it; others show the JSON as code.
`md(spec, frame=True)` writes a ```` ```{=html} ```` fence that holds a
sandboxed frame. leela draws this in a Markdown cell today, with no
change to leela.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rupaka/blob/main/rupaka/render.py#L140"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### md

``` python
def md(
    spec, frame:bool=False, height:int=760
)->str:
```

*A Markdown fence for `spec`: readable JSON, or a sandboxed frame.*

``` python
assert md(spec).startswith('```rupaka\n{') and json.loads(md(spec)[10:-4]) == spec
f = md(spec, frame=True)
assert f.startswith('```{=html}\n<iframe') and '<script' not in f and '&lt;script' in f
```

## FastHTML: Demo and Assets

`Demo(spec)` is the host element as an FT component. `Assets(prefix)`
gives the `Link` and the `Script` for a server that serves the bundle at
`prefix`. A server that shows scenes also serves `bundle('three')` as
`three.js` at the same prefix. The runtime loads it from there the first
time that a scene mounts, and only then.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rupaka/blob/main/rupaka/render.py#L151"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>
